originalIssue.message: 释义和提示反复把 astronaut 限定为执行太空任务的人，范围偏窄。受训宇航员在首次飞行前也可使用这一称呼；某些语境也包括非职业太空旅行者。应在同一个核心义内说明，并补充相应用例。

originalIssueResolutions.resolution: The main meaning now includes trained personnel before a first flight and qualifies broader non-professional travellers. The added private astronaut example is consistent with the broad dictionary sense. The mnemonic depicts one concrete mission scene without defining every astronaut by it.

originalIssue.message: 把中文译名“太空人”归为“美国语境”混淆了英语使用语境与中文译名习惯。

originalIssueResolutions.resolution: The definition no longer assigns the Chinese translation 太空人 to American English as if it were an English regional label.

originalIssue.message: space astronaut 通常冗余，不宜作为本义唯一的常用搭配教授。

originalIssueResolutions.resolution: Redundant space astronaut was replaced with astronaut training, a normal noun modifier combination.

originalIssue.message: 这里使用 an 的原因是 astronaut 为单数可数名词且以元音音素开头，不能概括为职业或身份前都用 an。

originalIssueResolutions.resolution: The an note now gives the singular countable noun and initial vowel sound as the reason.

originalIssue.message: 原列美式读音可以接受，但英美差异不只涉及重音标记；还应交代常见美式词尾 /nɑːt/，避免把 au 一律讲成 /ɔː/。

originalIssueResolutions.resolution: The accent note permits both American final vowels and explains that secondary-stress notation varies; Merriam-Webster independently confirms these variants.

originalIssue.message: Cambridge 页面未取得内容，不能作为此次释义、读音、辨析及词族说明的材料依据。可用的法语维基词典资料实际是英语词条，可支持名词释义和复数；其他说明不应挂接未取得的来源。

originalIssueResolutions.resolution: Unavailable Cambridge was removed from asserted source bindings. The saved English Wiktionary section supports noun and plural, while fresh independent Oxford/Merriam-Webster evidence supports the broader semantic and pronunciation checks.

linguisticFindings.detail: The single core person sense covers professional/trainee usage and the qualified broader traveller use. All seven structured examples and translations were read, including the self-paid private traveller. No new dictionary sense is invented for a different noun phrase.

The plural and an article are correct. American final vowel alternatives are acknowledged. Cosmonaut is a naming/use comparison, and ground crew is explicitly only a role contrast. Astronomy is a study field, not an astronaut derivative.

Astro- and nautēs are now in one parallel-components stage, followed by the English compound. Fresh Etymonline and Merriam-Webster support these meanings; the diagram no longer says star became sailor.

Astronautical is a legitimate related adjective; the lesson labels its technical register. The memory scene is illustrative, while the main definition expressly allows a trained person who has yet to fly.

sourceEvidence.text: Astronaut was formed using Greek-derived elements: astro- relating to stars and nautēs meaning sailor. The space-traveller term appeared in speculative writing before actual human spaceflight and was later popularized by the United States space programme. This is a modern formation from older elements, not an ancient Greek word for a modern occupation.
